rows.note: This is the all-purpose casual choice for a person or idea described as crazy, though it is not normally praise.

example.english: You’re insane if you think you can build a house in a week.
example.traditional: 你話要一個禮拜內起好間屋，真係黐線喎。
example.jyutping: nei5 waa6 jiu3 jat1 go3 lai5 baai3 noi6 hei2 hou2 gaan1 uk1 zan1 hai6 ci1 sin3 wo3

rows.note: Use this for a plan, claim, or situation that is outrageously unreasonable or impractical.

example.english: This plan requires every citizen to donate a hundred thousand dollars; it’s insane.
example.traditional: 呢個計劃要每個市民捐十萬蚊，真係離譜。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 gai3 waak6 jiu3 mui5 go3 si5 man4 gyun1 sap6 maan6 man1 zan1 hai6 lei4 pou2

rows.note: Use this approvingly for an extreme performance or ability, such as someone being unbelievably good at a game.

example.english: Their gaming is insane—they can even beat world champions.
example.traditional: 佢打機勁到癲，連世界冠軍都贏到。
example.jyutping: keoi5 daa2 gei1 ging6 dou3 din1 lin4 sai3 gaai3 gun3 gwan1 dou1 jeng4 dou2

rows.jyutping: zing1 san4 beng6 jan4 zyun1 jung6
rows.note: Use this in labels or descriptions for something intended specifically for people with mental illness.

example.english: This activity room is for insane people only.
example.traditional: 呢個活動室係精神病人專用。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 wut6 dung6 sat1 hai6 zing1 san4 beng6 jan4 zyun1 jung6
